method: Source-confirmed binding defects in public BUIDL CTC submissions, each read in the re-cloned repository and, where possible, corroborated by a live keyless probe or the ThirdCheck analyzer. Named; the private basis for responsible disclosure. Public materials describe the anti-pattern without the author until disclosure is acknowledged.

confirmed.summary: Every registration path verifies through IUSCVerifier.verifySingle / verifyBatch at 0x0FD2, selectors the precompile does not implement, and the verifier is an unguarded swappable address with a mock shipped in src/.
evidence: contracts/src/creditcoin/VaultLending.sol:160 calls IUSCVerifier(target).verifySingle on every registration path
contracts/src/creditcoin/MockStreakPrecompile.sol:10 mock returning true shipped in src/
proof-pipeline/src/generateAbsenceProof.ts:125 blanks the proof on failure but returns success:true
confirmed.liveProof: npm run judge:verify shows 0x0FD2 replies 'Unknown selector' to verifySingle while dispatching verify

confirmed.class: protocol proof replaced by a centralized signature
confirmed.summary: Presents itself as an Attestcoin consumer but verifies its 'attestation' with an off-chain ECDSA signature (ecrecover) against an owner-set validator, and never calls the precompile anywhere in the repo. Credit limits are set on that signature; a compromised or malicious validator key mints arbitrary credit.
evidence: src/contracts/SovereignAttestLending.sol:60 executeAttestedCredit sets userCreditLimits on the signature alone
no verify / verifyAndEmit / calculateTxIndex / 0x0FD2 reference anywhere in the repository
confirmed.liveProof: n/a (source fact); the ThirdCheck analyzer flags it as 'Attestation verified by signature, not the precompile'
confirmed.reproduce: npm run conformance is unrelated; scan with the analyzer: analyzeTree over the cloned repo yields the B-11 signature-not-precompile finding
